strengths: Exemplary ablation study (Table 1) systematically demonstrates the value of each component with clear empirical evidence for nonlinear compression over PCA and synergistic local-global-latent modeling
Strong empirical results: 60.9% FID improvement over SiT-B/2 baseline; reaches 1M-step REG performance (2.7 FID) with ~30% fewer iterations; consistent gains across model scales and generation modes
Semantic preservation validated beyond FID: attentive probing (Fig. 4) and semantic segmentation experiments (Fig. 6) demonstrate nonlinear compressor preserves VFM information better than PCA

Thorough design analysis: compression dimensionality (Fig. 5), model capacity (Table 5), VFM layer selection (Table 6), and cross-VFM robustness (Table 8) provide comprehensive justification for choices
Practical efficiency: negligible parameter increase (130M→132M), lightweight compressor (16.6M params), maintains inference efficiency with minimal throughput reduction
Clear presentation: well-written with informative figures/tables; reproducibility supported by detailed appendices and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core contribution is primarily engineering—replacing PCA with standard CNN autoencoder and concatenating three modalities. Semantic compressor is basic (3-layer CNN); external alignment loss from prior work. Lacks fundamental innovation

Restricted experimental scope: single dataset (ImageNet) and resolution (256×256) only; no higher-resolution experiments despite mentioning them; limited to ImageNet for unconditional generation; scope acknowledged as resource-constrained but limits generalizability

Unfair baseline comparisons: Table 4 compares 160-epoch REGLUE against 800-epoch REPA/ReDi/REG (5× difference); paper acknowledges but claims competitiveness anyway; no error bars or confidence intervals on FID scores

Missing theoretical understanding: no explanation for why nonlinear compression fundamentally outperforms PCA; no information-theoretic analysis; optimal 16-channel choice lacks principled justification; mechanisms of improvement unexplained

Heavy VFM dependency with limited robustness: CLIP-L significantly underperforms (18.1 vs. 12.9 FID); no analysis of what makes certain VFMs suitable; method cannot work without strong pretrained VFMs; cross-VFM generalization unclear

Incomplete computational cost analysis: while parameters constant, actual training/inference overhead not fully quantified; Table 5 shows throughput degrades substantially (32,304→9,510 samples/sec) with larger compressors; cost implications for practitioners unclear

Hyperparameter complexity without full sensitivity analysis: multiple hyperparameters (compression channels, hidden size, VFM layers, λs, λcls, λrep); different alignment layers across model sizes; limited exploration of full sensitivity space

Scalability limitations: XL/2 experiments limited to 1M steps due to resources; ultra-long training behavior unknown; no exploration of truly large models; limits assessment of method's utility for future large-scale systems

Limited negative results and failure analysis: no discussion of scenarios where joint modeling hurts; when linear compression suffices; failure modes beyond resource constraints; conditions for applicability undefined

State-of-the-art gaps not deeply analyzed: autoregressive models (VAR, MAR) outperform on FID (Table 4); fundamental performance gaps versus LDMs not discussed; positioning relative to future paradigms unclear

strengths: Excellent ablation study (Table 1) systematically decomposing contributions of local/global semantics, linear/non-linear compression, and external alignment; clearly shows patch-level spatial semantics outperform global-only signals

Efficient design maintaining inference-time throughput (3.8 img/s, same as REG) through channel-wise fusion, avoiding quadratic attention cost of concatenation while achieving significant FID improvements (60.9% over vanilla SiT-B/2)

Comprehensive semantic preservation analysis with probing accuracy (Figure 2), diffusability diagnostic showing high-frequency suppression (Figure 3), and semantic segmentation validation (68.7 mIoU with 16-channel compression vs 72.5 full features)

Thorough experimental validation across multiple metrics (FID, sFID, IS, Precision, Recall, CMMD, FD), both conditional/unconditional generation, model scales (B/XL), datasets (ImageNet, Food-101, ImageNet-512), and data-limited regimes with extensive ablations

Practical value of 30% training iteration reduction to match baseline performance; well-positioned for practitioners; promised code release and sufficient implementation details support reproducibility

Clear insights that non-linear compression significantly outperforms linear PCA with multiple layers (14.3 vs 21.4 FID over ReDi) and that patch-level spatial guidance is critical despite external alignment being complementary
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: joint VAE-latent + VFM-feature modeling already demonstrated by ReDi, multi-layer feature aggregation is straightforward concatenation, global [CLS] + alignment borrowed from REG; main contribution (non-linear compressor) is an engineering optimization rather than fundamental advance

Semantic compressor design lacks principled justification: no exploration of alternative architectures (transformer-based, knowledge distillation), unclear why 256 hidden dimensions is optimal beyond empirical ablation, connection between diffusability (Figure 3) and generation quality is empirical rather than analytical

Incomplete understanding of failure modes: setting (j) multi-layer PCA yields 23.1 FID versus 13.3 for non-linear multi-layer—a 9.8 FID gap warranting deeper investigation; setting (f) global-only alignment degrades performance, but mechanism ('unstable without spatial anchors') is superficial; why channel-wise addition outperforms alternatives lacks semantic justification

Limited evaluation scope: primarily ImageNet 256×256; XL experiments capped at 1M iterations (not ultra-long 4M training); no evaluation on other domains (COCO, artistic images) or generalization to non-SiT diffusion frameworks

Significant dependency on VFM quality underexplored: CLIP-L performs substantially worse (18.1 FID) than DINOv2-B (12.9); which VFM properties are essential (dimensionality, self-supervised pretraining) unclear, limiting transferability

Missing sensitivity analyses: no ablation on loss weights (λs=1, λcls=0.03, λrep=0.5), noise schedule interactions with semantic guidance unexplored, CFG ablations only for one configuration, compressor hidden dimensionality optimized empirically without principled explanation

Comparison framing concerns: main results mix different training epochs (REG/ReDi 800 epochs vs REGLUE 80 in Table 4); '30% fewer iterations' claim should specify regime (1M-step, SiT-XL/2 context); efficiency gains are real but narrative could be more precise

Technical clarity issues: dense notation in Section 3.2 could be simplified; semantic justification for channel-wise fusion (Eq. 5) is missing (justified only by efficiency); 'entanglement' framing oversells what is essentially feature fusion; critical details (compressor training) relegated to appendix
